- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and model rises sharply, it’s likely overconfident; apply downward bias of 3–5% to forecast.
- If model forecast mean is consistently above true outcome, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% from forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before applying sentiment-adjusted correction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model may misread trend direction; align forecast with sentiment’s recent 3-day moving average.
